To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the structures and processes that facilitate integration are not clearly delineated in Bennett et al.’s framework, (2) the structures and process of interdisciplinary research are essential for integration, and (3) the synergism of structures and processes is necessary for the success of interdisciplinary conservation research.
(1) Bennett et al. present a framework for interdisciplin ary research in conservation, and (2) their framework is lacking in the explanation of structures and processes.

the synergistic relationship of structures and processes creates an environment hospitable to integration, and that this environment is critical to the successful inclusion of the social sciences in interdisciplinary research.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how structures and processes can help facilitate integration and how these structures and processes can be designed to promote integration in conservation.
the role of structures and processes in facilitating integration.
the role structures and processes play in facilitating the integration of social and natural science in conservation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
“integration of the social and natural science is essential to conservation, and it is the responsibility of all conservationists to make it happen” (Bennett et al., 2016, 1).
the structures and processes of interdisciplinarily are necessary for the successful integration of the social and natural science.
the framework proposed by Bennett et al. has potential to be a powerful tool for integrating social and natural science in conservation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are working on a new way to understand the social and natural world, which we call “social-ecological systems” or SES.
we have been trying to develop an approach to integrating social and natural science in the field of conservation.
we have developed a framework for a collaborative and interor transdisciplinary conservation science and practice that is based on the principles of the social sciences.
The main takeaway from our work is that

conservationists must be cognizant of and intentional about the structures and processes necessary to facilitate interdisciplinary integration and mainstreaming of the social sciences in their research and practice.
conservation scientists and practitioners need to be cognizant of the role of structures and processes in interdisciplinary research and the need for both in order for integration to be effective.

the integration of disciplines is not a simple matter of adding more people to a project, but rather it is a complex, dynamic process that is best facilitated by structures and processes that support integration.
